newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lebed sacking dangerous mistake - German analyst.
newsitem.headline: Lebed sacking dangerous mistake - German analyst.

text.p: A German analyst said President Boris Yeltsin's decision to sack Alexander Lebed as Russia's national security adviser on Thursday was a major political mistake which could endanger the fragile peace in Chechnya.

"This whole peace process was connected with the personality of Lebed," Alexander Rahr, a Russian specialist at the German Society for Foreign Policy, told Reuters. "The danger is now that the situation could return to how it was before -- war."
"This decision was surely forced on Yeltsin by his entourage. Yeltsin himself has rarely made a political mistake and this seems to be a very big political mistake."
Rahr said he believed Lebed's power had become too great for some members of Yeltsin's inner circle.
The German Foreign Ministry declined to comment on Yeltsin's decision. A spokesman said the ministry did not comment on foreign government reshuffles.
Rahr said there was a danger that Interior Minister Anataly Kulikov, who has large numbers of elite troops under his command, could take charge of matters in Chechnya.
"We know what Kulikov's methods are... military force and absolutely no compromise," Rahr said.
